title: Metric drop hunting playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for on-call engineers to investigate sudden metric drops, missing instrumentation, and correlated noisy alerts that cause SLO burn or pager storms. It focuses on pragmatic, reproducible steps you can run from an on-call laptop or jumpbox and short-term mitigations to quiet noise without losing signal.

Why this is different:
- Not a generic alert-tuning doc — concentrates on "metric drop" patterns (eg. counters going to zero, histograms flattening), where instrumentation or export paths are failing rather than actual traffic loss.
- Includes signal-forensics checks that span application, collector, and ingestion layers.
- Prioritizes reversible mitigations for production: throttling alerting rules, short-term synthetic traffic, and circuit-breaker style fallback to a backup metric export.

Recent examples that motivated this playbook:
- 2026-01-14 03:20 UTC: Authentication success count for hosted-api dropped to zero for 7 minutes while latency and request traces remained healthy. Root cause: mis-deployed collector config (Prometheus relabel drop) from an infra PR. Pager volume: 18 pages.
- 2025-10-06 15:05 UTC: SLO burn on embedding throughput after dedup worker upgrade. Observed: worker metrics vanished due to a metrics key rename in code; aggregation pipeline treated missing keys as zeros. Pager noise amplified by composite alert using zero-fill.

First 10 minutes (initial triage checklist) — do these in parallel where possible:
1) Confirm symptom: check dashboards that are independently instrumented.
   - Is request traffic truly zero across metrics (ingress, network, traces)?
   - Run quick trace search for recent requests: `curl -s \"https://tracing.redwood.internal/api/v1/search?q=service:api AND @timestamp:>now-10m\"`
2) Check ingestion pipeline health:
   - Collector logs (hosted / sidecar): `kubectl -n observability logs -l app=metrics-collector --tail=200`
   - Prometheus targets: `curl -s http://prometheus.svc:9090/api/v1/targets` — look for DOWN or dropped targets/label mismatches
3) Check exporter/SDK versions: recent deploys? `git log --since='2h' --oneline` against service repo, look for instrumentation changes or dependency bumps.
4) Look for recent config PRs/deploys in infra: `JIRA-` tickets, CICD status, and rollout windows.
5) If rules use zero-fill or default on missing metrics, identify affected alerts and temporarily silence them (see quieting section).

Deeper signal-forensics (20–60 minutes) — rule out layers in this order:
A) Application instrumentation:
   - Are metrics keys/names changed? Grep recent commits for `counter(\"` or `histogram(\"` usages.
   - Check local SDK logs for metric emission errors (rate-limited errors, buffer overflow).
   - If app runs on many pods, check a few recent pod logs `kubectl logs -n svc svc-123 -c app --tail 500` for insta-errors from the instrumentation client.
B) Collector/agent:
   - Confirm configuration: relabel rules, scrape intervals, and filters. A common mistake: relabel rule accidentally drops the metric or removes a crucial label causing it to fall out of a recording rule.
   - Snapshot exporter health (queue lengths, retries).
C) Ingestion/TSDB:
   - Look for ingestion error spikes in the metric store (`/api/v1/series` responses, ingester error logs).
   - Check downsampling/rollup jobs and any recent schema migrations.

Quick mitigations to stop noise (do fast, reversible actions):
- Silence specific alert rules for 30–60 minutes with a note: "temp-silence metric-drop-investigation by <oncall>". Prefer rule-only silences over team-wide paging silence.
- If collector relabeling broke, rollback the collector config rollout (canary) or switch the service to the previous config via `kubectl rollout undo` in the observability namespace.
- If metric keys were renamed by a code change, restore the old key with a short-lived shim in app or an adapter in the collector to translate names.
- Synthetic traffic: if you suspect missing synthetic checks, add a low-rate synthetic that hits the endpoint and emits a stable metric until fully fixed.

Escalation and communication:
- Escalate to Observability lead when: (a) ingestion errors > 1% for > 10m, (b) SLO burn > 5% and > 15 minutes, or (c) inability to identify root layer after 30 minutes.
- Post a brief status in #sre-ops with: what we see, who is working, mitigations applied, ETA for next update.

Instrument-level hardening recommendations (post-incident fixes):
- Avoid zero-fill in composite alerts; instead use absence detection and explicit missing-data alerting.
- Add redundancy: emit the same critical counter from two independent pipelines (app SDK and gateway layer) so a single collector or SDK bug doesn't zero out both.
- Add a schema compatibility check in CI for metric name/type changes (block PRs that change existing metric names without a compatibility flag).
- Add unit tests that validate metric keys in smoke-tests and run on deploy gates.

Long-term platform changes to reduce noise/signal gaps:
- Store ingestion deltas (ingested samples per metric per minute) as a separate dataset and alert on ingestion drop rather than metric value zero.
- Implement a short-lived circuit-breaker pattern in alerts: require a secondary corroborating signal (traces or gateway success count) before paging.

Postmortem checklist (for a full incident):
- Create postmortem ticket within 48h and tag `obs-metric-drop`
- Collect artifacts: screenshots of dashboards, raw exporter logs (first 60m), git commits for deploys during window, and alert history.
- Action items: assign owners, due dates, and link PRs for fixes; schedule a 1:1 with infra owner if rollout config caused the incident.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Implement `metric-schema-check` in CI (owner: Elena, ETA: 2026-03-10).
- Evaluate feasibility of dual-emission for `auth_success_total` and other high-value counters (owner: Raj, ETA: 2026-04-01).
- Prototype ingestion-delta dataset and eviction alerts (owner: Samir).

Notes to on-call engineers:
- When in doubt, silence the specific rule with an annotation and prefer short duration; better to have a quieter page storm and collect for postmortem than escalate every transient noise spike.
- Document steps you took in the alert thread (timestamps + commands) so follow-on shifts can pick up quickly.

References and useful commands:
- Prometheus targets: `curl -s http://prometheus.svc:9090/api/v1/targets | jq .`
- Check series presence: `curl -s \"http://prometheus.svc:9090/api/v1/series?match[]=auth_success_total&start=$(date -u -d '10 minutes ago' +%s)\"`
- Example silence command (PagerDuty): `pd-api silence create --service_id SVC123 --duration 60 --summary 'temp-silence metric drop investigation'`

End of playbook — please update this doc when you discover a new diagnostic trick or after an incident. Keep entries concise; add links to PRs and postmortems in the linked_artifacts list.
